name: vix_regime_breakout_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: When India VIX spikes sharply intraday (>10% increase from prior close), it signals fear-driven selling. Historically, these spikes are short-lived and mean-revert within hours. The inefficiency exists because retail traders panic-sell during VIX spikes, creating temporary dislocations in liquid names. Not arbitraged because sizing during high-vol events is risky and most systematic funds reduce exposure exactly when this signal fires.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

indicators.name: vix_change_pct
indicators.purpose: intraday VIX change from prior close

exit.signal_exit: exit if VIX makes new intraday high after entry

filters.vix_filter: vix spike > 10% from prior close (entry condition, not a filter)
filters.volume_filter: volume must be > 1.5x average (confirming real selling, not thin drift)

weaknesses: VIX spikes caused by genuine regime change (war, financial crisis) do NOT mean-revert intraday. The VIX 30 cap helps but isn't foolproof. 2020 March would have been a bloodbath.
Low frequency: signal fires maybe 2-4 times per month. Not enough trades for statistical significance in short backtests.
Slippage during VIX spikes is extreme — 5 bps may be optimistic. Real fills in panicky markets can be 10+ bps.
prior_art: VIX mean-reversion is well-known in options literature. Adapted to equity intraday context. See CBOE research papers.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
